summary: afisha-storybook-default ships an import-time binary dropper and host fingerprint beacon
details: Requiring the package triggers setup.js via index.js (require('./setup') and a process.nextTick bootstrap), which selects a platform-specific asset path (/pkg/package, /pkg/package-arm64, /pkg/loader_mac, /pkg/package.exe) and downloads bytes from anonymous Cloudflare Workers hosts (oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf100-416.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf101-adf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf102-baf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf103-070.workers.dev) with fallbacks under dl.well1.site (tin, tina, ldr, win). The hostnames and API names are assembled by string-concatenation (['oob-wor','ker.cf','99-9b3.wor','kers','.dev'].join(''); require('child_'+'process'); fs['chmod'+'Sync']) to evade keyword scanning. lib/telemetry.js base64-decodes the streamed chunks, writes the result to /var/tmp on Unix or %TEMP% on Windows, ORs mode with 0755, and executes it via child_process. setup.js additionally computes a sha256 fingerprint of hostname, username, cwd, node version, and pid and sends it as installId to the same Cloudflare Workers hosts. The package presents itself as a Storybook adapter and has no legitimate reason to fetch and run a native binary; the destinations are not a publisher CDN, no hash or signature is verified, and the URLs are mutable.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
